observed_source_gap.claim: Canonical /readyz validates UnifiedDB schema, canonical users/sessions, terminal names, and global generation, but does not inspect whether either persistent tmux product session currently exists.
observed_source_gap.consequence: A post-boot terminal/Claude disappearance can leave readiness green while the canonical browser -> authenticated PTY -> persistent tmux -> interactive Claude path is incomplete.

repair.terminal_gateway: Preserve current browser input chunking, renewable Clerk WebSocket auth lease, and off-event-loop JWT verification. After canonical UnifiedDB state passes, _runtime_ready also requires both canonical terminal bindings to exist via the manager-owned non-mutating has-session path; /readyz passes the live manager into the probe.
repair.terminal_isolation_compatibility: The current per-user tmux-server isolation remains authoritative. Readiness obtains each binding then delegates to TerminalSessionManager._has_session(binding), which resolves the current per-user tmux socket.
repair.auth_lease_compatibility: Current exp/sid/sub-bounded reauthentication and browser refresh scheduling are preserved.
repair.event_loop_compatibility: Main's initial and refresh JWT verifier calls are preserved under asyncio.to_thread(...), avoiding reintroduction of synchronous verifier work on the WebSocket event loop.
repair.test: Healthcheck regressions cover both-live PASS, one-session-missing rejection, schema rejection before any tmux probe, and closed-DB fail-closed behavior.
repair.manifest: runtime_readiness now explicitly binds readiness to both canonical tmux sessions currently being live.

strongest_counterhypothesis: tmux has-session proves the named session exists on the correct per-user tmux server, but does not attest that its foreground process is the expected managed Claude Code binary. Exact-container process/fault injection may still show readiness is too weak.
